property_summary: The value of MinSum must never change after the contract is initialized.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum is the same as the initial MinSum set by SetMinSum.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum must not have changed (i.e., MinSum remains equal to its initial value set during deployment and never modified after).
After any call to Collect, MinSum equals the value set during the only allowed SetMinSum call (i.e., before Initialized is called).
After any Collect call that succeeds (does not revert), MinSum must not change.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum must equal its value after SetMinSum is called with a non-initialized contract.

After any sequence of calls that includes a call to SetMinSum with initialized==true, the value of MinSum must be the last value passed to a successful SetMinSum call, i.e., it must not change when the contract is already initialized.

After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the value of MinSum must be the value set by the only successful SetMinSum call (if any), and must not change from the initial value 0 if SetMinSum was never called successfully.
The value of MinSum is unchanged after any call to Collect.
The value of MinSum must equal the value passed to the first successful SetMinSum call.
After a Collect call that succeeds, MinSum is unchanged from its initial value of 0.
After any successful Collect call, MinSum remains equal to the last value set by SetMinSum.
After any call to Collect, MinSum is unchanged from its value before the call.
After any call to Collect, MinSum retains the value it had before the call.
After a successful Collect call, MinSum is unchanged from its value before the call.
After Collect, the LogFile address set by SetLogFile remains unchanged regardless of whether Initialized was called.
After Collect, the address of LogFile as returned by the public getter LogFile() is always the address set by SetLogFile, even if SetLogFile was called after Initialized.
The LogFile address returned by the public getter LogFile() equals the address set by the last call to SetLogFile, even if SetLogFile is called after Initialized.
The LogFile address remains unchanged after Collect() regardless of whether Initialized was called.
After Collect() reverts, the LogFile address is exactly the address set by SetLogFile, even if SetLogFile is called after Initialized.
After Collect(uint256) returns successfully, the locked_ state (observed via a second call reverting) is false.
After Collect(uint256) returns without revert, a subsequent call to the nonReentrant function Initialized() succeeds (i.e., does not revert).
After a successful Collect(uint256) call, the function Initialized() can be called without reverting, but in the buggy version it reverts because the reentrancy lock persists.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the bool state that controls initialization is true.
After a successful call to Collect(uint256), Initialized() returns true (the contract is still usable because the reentrancy lock is released).

After a call to Collect, the accumulated balance of msg.sender (c.Acc(msg.sender).balance) is at most the previous value (accounting for possible previous balance and any ether sent in the call), and the unlockTime is never decreased.
After Collect is called by msg.sender with amount _am, the balance of msg.sender in the contract is either unchanged (if call reverted) or decreased by exactly _am (if call succeeded).
After a Collect call, the unlock time of the caller is never increased to a value strictly greater than the block timestamp plus the lock time of any previous Put call.
After a call to Put, the unlockTime for msg.sender is strictly greater than the sum of block.timestamp and _lockTime (i.e., only updated if that sum is greater, not equal).
After a call to Collect, the unlockTime of the caller is never strictly less than block.timestamp plus _lockTime of the last Put call.
After a Collect call, the unlocked time for the sender is always greater than or equal to the timestamp (i.e., it never decreases).

After Collect, the sender's unlock time equals the old unlock time (since Put's lock time update is missing in M). In P, the unlock time never changes except when Put is called; in M, the unlock time never changes at all. The rule: calling Collect does not change the unlock time of msg.sender.
After Collect fails because balance is less than MinSum, the caller's balance remains unchanged.
After calling Collect, the unlockTime of the sender remains unchanged.
After calling Collect(uint256), the sender's balance is less than or equal to their balance before the call.
After Collect(uint256) succeeds, the caller's balance in Acc decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn, while the contract's ether balance decreases by the same amount.
After Collect(uint256) reverts, the locked_ state variable remains false, allowing a subsequent nonReentrant call to proceed.
After Collect(uint256) succeeds, the sender's balance in Acc decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After Collect(uint256) succeeds, the contract's ether balance decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After Collect(uint256) reverts, the locked_ state variable remains false and the caller's balance in Acc is unchanged.
